I did not run Lean, so I don't know whether `mem_ker_piQuotient` actually fails to fire. The competition rests on `MonoidHom.mem_ker` being `@[simp]` and matching the same left-hand side. `piQuotient_apply` looks fine: it is a rfl lemma that rewrites to the quotient `mk` and does not loop. findings.excerpt:
theorem mem_ker_piQuotient (s : Finset I) (N : ∀ i : s, Subgroup (G i))
    [∀ i : s, (N i).Normal] (x : ∀ i, G i) :
    x ∈ (piQuotient s N).toMonoidHom.ker ↔ ∀ i : s, x i ∈ N i := by
findings.problem: The `@[simp]` lemma is stated on `x ∈ (piQuotient s N).toMonoidHom.ker`. That left-hand side is also matched by Mathlib's simp lemma `MonoidHom.mem_ker : x ∈ f.ker ↔ f x = 1`. The two compete, and `mem_ker_piQuotient` is not guaranteed to be the one that fires. If `MonoidHom.mem_ker` wins, the goal becomes `piQuotient s N x = 1`, which has no simp rule. So the cylinder characterization may never be reached by `simp`, and the `@[simp]` attribute is unreliable. The proof itself begins with `change piQuotient (G := G) s N x = 1 ↔ _`, which shows the natural normal form. The only downstream uses I found, in the test file and in `exists_finset_openNormalSubgroup_pi_factor`, call the lemma by hand with `.mp`. Nothing relies on simp applying it.
findings.proposed_change: Add a simp lemma on the normal form that simp reaches after `MonoidHom.mem_ker`: `@[simp] theorem piQuotient_eq_one_iff (s) (N) [∀ i : s, (N i).Normal] (x : ∀ i, G i) : piQuotient s N x = 1 ↔ ∀ i : s, x i ∈ N i`. Its proof is the existing body without the initial `change`. Then either drop `@[simp]` from `mem_ker_piQuotient` or keep it as a non-simp wrapper that derives from the new lemma. Either way, the rewrite route goes through `MonoidHom.mem_ker` and then the new lemma, with no competing rules.
findings.benefit: `simp` can then turn kernel membership or `piQuotient s N x = 1` into the coordinatewise condition `∀ i : s, x i ∈ N i`. This works whether or not the goal is phrased through `.toMonoidHom.ker`. Users no longer need manual `.mp`/`.mpr` applications, as the test file does. The simp set also no longer depends on which of two overlapping rules fires first.
